title: Fix benchmark regression/variance caused by decode-loop debug logging
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Title: Fix benchmark regression/variance caused by decode-loop debug logging

Context
We traced the p95 jitter/throughput regression seen in the FP8/INT8 matrix runner (especially H100 decode-heavy cases) to a debug logging path that was accidentally left enabled in the “benchmark” execution mode. The logging was on the hot path (per-step / per-batch) and was also triggering extra string formatting + mutex contention in spdlog sinks. This perturbed kernel scheduling enough to show as benchmark variance and, in a few cases, flipped the apparent winner between baseline vs quantized paths.

This PR removes the hot-path debug logs from the decode loop and gates the remaining instrumentation behind an explicit opt-in flag that is OFF by default in all benchmark runners.

What changed
- Remove per-iteration debug logs in decode loop (token step) and prefill inner loop.
- Keep a small amount of high-level progress logging (once per request / once per batch) at INFO.
- Add an explicit runtime flag and env gate for verbose benchmark logging:
  - CLI: --bench_debug_logging (default: false)
  - Env: RW_BENCH_DEBUG_LOGGING=1 (only honored when --bench_debug_logging=true)
  - Rationale: accidental env-only enablement was too easy; we now require explicit CLI intent.
- Ensure benchmark harness forces these off:
  - benchmark runner now passes --bench_debug_logging=false explicitly
  - removed legacy RW_VERBOSE_BENCH_LOGS support (was enabling the path implicitly)
- Add a small guard macro around formatting-heavy debug code to avoid even evaluating fmt args when disabled.

Why this is safe
- Debug logging was not used for production runtime decisions; it was only intended for local troubleshooting.
- The new logging is opt-in and has a dedicated flag name to avoid collisions with existing --verbose / --log_level.
- No functional changes to kernel selection or scheduler behavior besides removing side effects.

Evidence / before & after
- Reproduced on H100 (decode-heavy workload: long generations, concurrency=32) using the matrix runner config from ENG-7428.
- Before:
  - tokens/s variance: ~9–13% run-to-run (same commit, same node)
  - p95 TPOT jitter spikes aligned with log sink backpressure
- After:
  - tokens/s variance: ~1.5–2.8% run-to-run
  - p95 TPOT stable; no spikes correlated with logging

Implementation notes
- We previously had a log statement inside the decode step loop that ran at DEBUG but the benchmark container set log_level=debug by default for an unrelated issue (trace collection). That effectively enabled the statement.
- The statement also used fmt::format with a couple of large structs (shape + scheduler state), which was costly even when the sink dropped messages.
- New code uses a fast boolean gate and avoids formatting work entirely unless explicitly enabled.

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/decode_loop.cc: remove per-step debug logging and guard remaining debug-only instrumentation
- runtime/bench/bench_flags.cc: add --bench_debug_logging flag and env validation
- tools/benchmark_runner/run_matrix.py: explicitly disable bench debug logging
- docs/internal/benchmarking.md: update “how to enable debug logs” section + note about perf impact

Illustrative snippet
Before:
  SPDLOG_DEBUG("decode step={} qdepth={} shapes={} ...", step, qdepth, shapes_to_string(...));
After:
  if (UNLIKELY(bench_debug_logging_enabled)) {
    SPDLOG_DEBUG("decode step={} qdepth={} shapes={} ...", step, qdepth, shapes_to_string(...));
  }

Commits
- runtime: remove decode hot-path debug logs
- runtime: add bench_debug_logging flag + env gate
- benchmark-runner: pass explicit default flags
- docs: update benchmarking debug logging guidance

Checklist
- [x] Reproduced variance regression on H100 and confirmed fix
- [x] Verified no change in outputs/correctness (same seeds, same prompts)
- [x] Confirmed matrix runner defaults keep logs OFF
- [x] Added note to internal benchmarking docs

Review conversation (highlights)
- Claire Dubois: “Can we make it impossible for env alone to enable this? Bench runners pick up env from CI sometimes.”
  - Rina: “Done. Env is only consulted if the CLI flag is explicitly set. Also removed the legacy env var that was used by older scripts.”
- Isabella Rossi: “Do we still have enough logging to debug harness failures?”
  - Rina: “Yes—request-level and batch-level logs remain at INFO. The per-step token logging is still available behind --bench_debug_logging for local repro only.”
- Noah Patel: “Please make sure formatting doesn’t happen when disabled (fmt args).”
  - Rina: “Added explicit gate before calling shapes_to_string; also added a small helper to keep the callsite clean.”

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- runtime-lint: PASS
- bench-smoke (A10): PASS

Merge
Squash merged to main. Follow-up: we should audit benchmark container defaults for log_level and make sure perf-canary jobs don’t run with DEBUG unless they are capturing traces (tracked under ENG-7429).
